questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be on high beam.
questions.explanation: Using high beam headlights during the day helps other drivers see you. Use high beam any time you are not following or approaching another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it signals they plan to turn right or change lanes to the right. This is a hand signal instead of a mechanical turn signal.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders in a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when entering curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. While staggered formation is good for staying close in a group, single-file is safer for curves.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, adjust the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Adjust tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for your load weight before riding.

questions.question: A larger space cushion may not be needed if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are poor, such as slippery pavement, heavy traffic, or limited visibility. A larger cushion is not needed only in perfect weather and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths: the left side, the center, and the right side.

questions.question: If you brake while turning in a curve:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction.
questions.explanation: When leaning into a curve, some tire traction is used for turning. This means less traction is available for braking, so braking in a curve requires extra care.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far right as possible.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving right increases collision risk. Moving left may cause the other driver to merge back too soon. The center position is safest.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the front of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay just behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind the group and lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see better, avoid blind spots, stay away from hazards, and provide an escape route. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure applied to them. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the motorcycle, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the motorcycle, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, straighten the motorcycle first and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes gently and gradually. Reduce your lean angle as you slow down, then press the brakes harder.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors help others see you. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Dark colors like black are not as good.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to make a turn. To lean the motorcycle the right way, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
There is no single best position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position for all situations.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Choose a lane position based on your riding conditions. Your position should give you enough space and help others see you.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a rider is how many times more likely to get a serious head injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing loss.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks important sounds like horns.
Do not use hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing loss, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs and other hearing protection prevent damage while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced. Bend your arms slightly when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: As a rider, what should you NOT tell a passenger to do before they ride with you?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount the motorcycle only after the engine starts. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: If you need to brake while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you finish the turn before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a turn, the tires have less grip than when the motorcycle is upright. Try to straighten the motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and gently, not hard like you would on a straight road.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol level (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect blood alcohol level: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake can also have an effect.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use headlights of other vehicles to help you see.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials to be more visible. Change your position in the lane as needed to see, be seen, and keep space around you.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both brakes when either one is used.
Remembers the rider's usual braking strength.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies partial front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Read your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your braking system.
